chunks: “Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, when a man stole for the first time, would cut off his right hand. If he returned to it, he would cut off his left foot. If he returned a third time, he would confine him permanently in prison and spend on him from the public treasury.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: the title of Imam 'Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام
key_terms.الصَّادِقُ: Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: What punishment did Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام apply for repeated theft?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling attributed to Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام regarding repeated theft, with escalating punishment across successive offenses. It also indicates that after permanent imprisonment for a third offense, the offender was to be maintained from the public treasury.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5111 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"When a man committed theft for the first time, Commander of the Faithful (as) would cut off his right hand. If he repeated the theft, he would cut off his left foot. If he stole a third time, he would imprison him for life and provide for him from the public treasury."
